answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost.
